pro_course_detail.title: Vocabulary :  Objects in the classroom
pro_course_detail.description:
Lesson Aims:
By the end of the lesson, student will be better able to Identify, understand and use the names of objects in the classroom.
Target vocabulary: Pencil, desk, rubber, ruler, blackboard, shelf, dictionary, bookcase, bin.
 The strategy used by me for this topic is PPP. I will start with warmer exercise first as this helps to set the tone for the lesson. For warmer activity a game called ‘Telling a story’ will be played. In this activity a picture is shown to the student and he need to make up a short story related to it.  This fun activity will help to gain attention of the student and activate him to participate in lesson. I will then move on to presentation stage, starting with meaning. During this stage, the target vocabulary i.e  objects in classroom with its meaning is introduced to the student using the flashcard and realia. At this stage student will be encouraged to speak in target language only.  CCQ’s will help me to ensure that student have understood the meaning of target vocabulary.
Next I will follow presentation (form) stage. In this student will be given word scramble worksheet pdf . I will check his worksheet for correct spelling. I will use chorus drilling to help the student with pronunciation of target vocabulary.  student will also be asked to complete Role play activity named “Classroom Designing/Requirements”. Model scenario written on the board will help him to complete this activity. This will provide the student with an opportunity to communicate or use the target language freely in a natural conversation. Finally during the cooler stage, I will conclude the lesson and end it on a positive note. This stage will reflect on new target vocabulary learnt by him. He will be given homework in which he need to practice pronunciation of vocabulary words taught in class.

teacher_info.teaching_style:
My focus is to help build confidence and fluency in English and help with your individual needs of pronunciation, grammar, vocabulary, reading, writing, listening and speaking.

Conversation is one of the best ways to begin "thinking directly" in English, and it removes the process of translating everything you want to say, and understand. We can have a relaxed conversation, you can ask questions, and use pictures, music or articles too. I want to help make things easier on your journey to your English goals.

pro_course_detail.description:
Here we can discuss any areas you need help with in the Speaking Part of the IELTS exam. There are different aspects of the scoring criteria, and we can work on understanding these, how your answers are impacted by them and how the answers can be improved to reach a higher band score. We can have practice tests of the Speaking Part of the IELTS exam, and afterwards discuss and analyze them to help bring about even further improvement.
